kept.title: Remote Code Execution via Dynamic Require
kept.description: The application uses user-controllable input to dynamically require modules, enabling arbitrary code execution.
steps_to_exploit: Identify a location where 'name' can be controlled via config files or CLI flags.
Provide a path to a malicious local JavaScript file.
The application executes the malicious code within the local process context.
kept.impact: Full system compromise with the privileges of the Node.js process.

kept.title: Prototype Pollution in Data Processing
kept.description: While a DANGEROUS_KEYS blacklist exists, it is insufficient to prevent all forms of prototype pollution in object manipulation routines.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a JSON input payload containing __proto__ or other hidden prototype chain keys.
Inject properties that affect application-wide behavior (e.g., modifying object prototypes used in logic).
Trigger logic that relies on object properties affected by the pollution.
kept.impact: Denial of service or logic manipulation across the application instance.

kept.title: Insecure Use of Unsafe Commands in CI/CD
kept.description: The CI/CD pipeline explicitly enables insecure commands, exposing the build environment to potential execution of malicious scripts.
steps_to_exploit: Compromise the repository or PR to include malicious code.
The CI/CD build runner processes the workflow which includes ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS: true.
Inject malicious commands into the build logs/output that the runner executes.
kept.impact: Compromise of the build/release pipeline or leaked environment secrets.

kept.title: Arbitrary File Read via Config Loading
kept.description: Functions loading configuration files via user-provided paths do not sufficiently constrain file access, potentially allowing reads of sensitive files outside intended directories.
steps_to_exploit: Supply a --config argument pointing to a sensitive file (e.g., /etc/passwd).
The application uses fs.readFileSync on the provided path without validation.
The content is parsed or logged, revealing sensitive information.
kept.impact: Unauthorized access to sensitive server-side files.

kept.title: Command Injection Risk in CLI Input
kept.description: User input for CLI arguments is not properly sanitized, potentially leading to command injection or command line option injection if passed to other shell-based tools.
steps_to_exploit: Provide malicious shell input characters in CLI flags.
The application fails to properly sanitize or validate the input in the argument parsing loop.
The malicious input is processed in a way that allows parameter tampering.
kept.impact: Execution of arbitrary commands or unintended tool behavior.

kept.title: Insecure Handling of Sensitive JSON Files
kept.description: The application blindly parses and uses JSON files from the filesystem which can lead to information disclosure or system manipulation if the file is attacker-controlled.
steps_to_exploit: Create or replace a browserlist-stats.json file with malicious data.
Run the application with a path argument pointing to the directory containing the malicious file.
The application reads and processes the attacker-controlled JSON.
kept.impact: Manipulation of browser usage statistics used for decision making.

kept.title: Denial of Service via Regex Complexity
kept.description: Regex patterns used for parsing queries are vulnerable to ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service) due to poor grouping and repetition.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a long, malicious string that matches parts of the regex but fails at the end.
Submit this string as a query to the CLI tool.
The process hangs or consumes excessive CPU, leading to Denial of Service.

kept.title: Weak Configuration Integrity via Sync File System Access
kept.description: The application relies on synchronous file system operations to locate and read configuration files, which can lead to race conditions or file-system-level DoS.
steps_to_exploit: Create a symbolic link attack to point config files to infinite loops or blocked character devices.
Execute the application.
The application hangs on synchronous operations.
kept.impact: Application instability and Denial of Service.

kept.title: Excessive Error Reporting Information Disclosure
kept.description: The application throws errors that can include local file system paths and internal state information, aiding in reconnaissance.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger an error by requesting a missing or invalid file/config.
Observe the stderr output containing internal absolute path details or environment specifics.
kept.impact: Exposure of server-side directory structures and internal file names.

kept.title: Insecure Default Version Assumptions
kept.description: Hardcoding default browser versions can lead to insecure baseline configurations if the environment or user expects more recent, safer standards.
steps_to_exploit: Rely on the default browser configuration provided by the tool.
The tool defaults to older versions which may contain known security vulnerabilities or lack modern security mitigations.
kept.impact: Deployment of applications that support browsers with known vulnerabilities.

kept.title: Path Traversal in Path Normalization
kept.description: While path checking exists, manual path joining and parent directory traversal logic is susceptible to complex path traversal attacks.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a path including '../' sequences.
The application, depending on the OS and Node version, might normalize the path improperly.
Gain access to unauthorized directories.
kept.impact: Unauthorized access to files outside the intended project directory.

kept.title: Lack of Strict Input Length Limits
kept.description: The CLI argument parser does not enforce a maximum length on query strings, allowing memory-exhaustion attacks.
steps_to_exploit: Submit a massive query string (several megabytes in size).
The application stores and processes this in memory.
The application crashes due to Out of Memory (OOM).

kept.title: Insecure Use of Shell Commands for Update DB
kept.description: The --update-db command suggests or relies on external scripts that may execute arbitrary commands if the path is manipulated.
steps_to_exploit: Manipulate the execution context/environment.
Trigger the update script which is handled by a side-effect-heavy function.
The underlying tool might execute arbitrary code if the environment is polluted.
kept.impact: Code execution on the developer machine.

kept.title: Improper Validation of Config Files
kept.description: The config file parser doesn't validate types thoroughly, allowing for unexpected object types to be introduced into the system state.
steps_to_exploit: Pass a specially crafted JSON object that misleads the parser.
Cause a type confusion in downstream processing logic.

kept.title: Unsafe Trust in Environment Variables
kept.description: Sensitive application flags are directly taken from environment variables without being properly scrubbed, which can be hijacked in shared environments.
steps_to_exploit: Set BROAD_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES for BROWSERSLIST_... in a shared container/shell.
The application consumes these as trusted configuration overrides.
The application behavior is altered by a malicious local user.
